convoLines.text: "What do you make of all this? Really."
"Bleak. Probably true. I keep looking for the part where it's not."
"a ridge with a view for miles — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"a spring that runs clear — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
They glance toward the fire, toward the others — checking who's listening.
"That's not — that's not what happened." Jae's hands won't stop moving. "You're twisting things."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Listen to me — Still on what you make of all this."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"I can't reach this properly. Could you clean it out for me? Please."
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Cooking With Teeth. They just... took Carlos. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"I save the best bite for last. It passes the time. The time passes anyway."
"The plan is the plan until it isn't. Then we make a new one."
"Anyway — I should get going."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can we talk?" Jae doesn't wait for an answer. "We need to discuss how things are run here."
"a cellar full of jars — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
Something crosses their face — quick, then gone. The practiced expression clicks back into place.
*They've deflected you before. The evidence needs to be heavier this time — one more thread before you speak.*
"Oh." A long pause. "I didn't think it was anyone's. It's gone — I ate it days ago. I'm sorry."
Their eyes do the math before their mouth does. You can see the calculation happening.
"I don't actually want to belong somewhere. I want to be in charge. Someone I love needed the lie more than I needed the truth."
"You're really going to make me say it again?" Jae rubs their face. "Fine — but it's the same truth as last time."
"That again?" Jae sighs. "I confessed that already. I'm not confessing it twice for dramatic effect."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"They took Carlos — Cooking With Teeth, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About this wound — still need hands. Are you in?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "They took Carlos — Cooking With Teeth, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them Wood Sorrel — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"...Actually, forget it."
"Can I tell you something? I'm practicing what I would say if I ever saw my family again. I haven't told anyone."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
"Here. I made an extra." Jae presses something into your hand — a decent tool, oiled and kept. (Useful. Keep it.)
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
"Don't tell anyone I told you. What's on your mind?"

"Huh. Let me think about that." "Last time things were different. They always are." "Have you heard what they're calling Flashbulb Moth? Jae is pushing 'Loud-Eyes'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
"Give it three more days of arguing. Then someone says the obvious thing and we all pretend it was theirs."
"Hear me out — Still on what's been happening."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Can we talk? Have you seen anyone on the roads? Anyone at all? I'm asking everyone."
They nod. "Okay."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Yeah? What's up?"

"Huh. Let me think about that." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "The whole fire was arguing about Flashbulb Moth last night — what to even CALL it. 'The Ugly Beast' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Like I said — Still on what's been happening."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"We never did finish talking about their secret — that was 10 days back. Still on your mind? 'Don't tell anyone I told you. What's on your mind?'"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"...Anyway. What did you want to ask?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "We lost Carlos, Hunter and Gerald. I do the headcount without thinking. Then I think."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on what's been happening. That's still where we are."
Something eases in their shoulders. They're really talking to you now.
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"Don't mind me. Today's just heavy."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
"I buried this before the Scattering. Seemed stupid to keep it secret." Lelisa digs up a wrapped bundle — food, still good. (+1481 kcal to the pantry.)
"You're kind. Don't let this place change that."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
"Sorry — I got lost in it for a second. What did you want to ask?"
"Carlos is gone, Hunter is gone, and Gerald is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"They're already drifting away. "Later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
"This was good." They mean it.
